name: whatsapp-mcp
description: Read WhatsApp on this Mac: chats, messages, calls, labels, the address book, and the files behind attachments — photos, PDFs, video frames, and voice notes transcribed on-device. It never changes WhatsApp and cannot send anything
long_description:
A local MCP server written in Swift that reads WhatsApp on this Mac.

Everything comes from WhatsApp's own local databases, opened read-only and immutable, and from the media files under WhatsApp's Message folder. On recent macOS, reading them needs Full Disk Access for this extension's program (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Full Disk Access → whatsapp-mcp), and the grant has to be given again after every update, because macOS ties it to the exact program. Without it the server says so, with the steps.

A reply shows the message it quotes and a message shows who reacted with which emoji; starred messages can be listed across every chat. Beyond messages it reads calls, live-location sessions, labels, WhatsApp's address book, channels and LID pairings; opens attachments (a photo as an image, a PDF as text, a video as frames); transcribes voice notes with the speech recognition built into macOS, entirely on this Mac; and offers one read-only SELECT over any allow-listed WhatsApp database. Key material and raw protocol queues are refused.

Read-only toward WhatsApp. There is no tool that sends, edits or deletes anything, no shortcut, and no route to any network — no model is ever downloaded.

The one thing it writes is its own cache, ~/Library/Caches/whatsapp-mcp: private copies of WhatsApp's databases, saved transcripts, and a scratch file deleted after each conversion. That cache holds real message data in plaintext, readable only by you, until you delete it.

Transcription needs macOS 26 or later, the language's speech model installed, and, ffmpeg (brew install ffmpeg) for a video's sound track and any container macOS cannot open itself — on macOS 27 that does not include WhatsApp's voice notes. macOS does not offer Basque or Catalan for this engine; the tool says so instead of guessing. Transcripts are automatic and can be wrong.

WhatsApp's data is private, undocumented storage that can change in any update, so this server checks its shape first and says plainly when it no longer matches — a schema change must not read as "you have no messages". Status updates are not covered.

Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to WhatsApp or Meta.

tools.name: whatsapp_status
tools.description: Reports whether WhatsApp's local database can be read, how much is in it, what WhatsApp does not store locally at all, and exactly what to do about anything missing. Reads no messages.

tools.name: chats_list
tools.description: Lists conversations with their id, kind, unread count, how many messages are stored, and when the last one arrived.

tools.name: chat_get
tools.description: Returns a page of messages from one chat, newest first by default, each line saying who sent it and what the message is — text, a photo, a voice note with its length, a sticker, a location, a link, a group event, or a deletion.

tools.name: whatsapp_search
tools.description: Finds messages whose text contains a phrase, across every chat or within one. Matching ignores case and accents, so "angel" finds "Ángel". With starred_only the phrase can be left out to list every starred message.

tools.name: message_get
tools.description: Everything this database holds about one message: mentions, both timestamps, an attachment's path, size, length, author and WhatsApp URL, a shared contact's full vCard, a link preview, a group event's actor and subject, the message it replies to, who reacted with which emoji, and the raw delivery and error codes.

tools.name: media_list
tools.description: Lists what was shared rather than said: photos, videos, GIFs, stickers, voice notes, audio files, documents, shared locations and shared contact cards, with the message id each belongs to and the file's path on this Mac when it is here.

tools.name: group_get
tools.description: What this server can read about a group: when it was created and by whom, when its name last changed, and every member row with its address, resolved name and admin flag.

tools.name: media_get
tools.description: Facts about the file behind one attachment: its real path, MIME type, exact size, SHA-256, and the chat, sender and date. Says plainly when the file is not on this Mac.

tools.name: media_view
tools.description: Shows what is inside an attachment: a photo or sticker as an image, a PDF or text document as text, a video as still frames. Audio is transcribed with audio_transcribe.

tools.name: audio_transcribe
tools.description: Turns a voice note, audio file or a video's sound into text with times, using the speech recognition built into macOS, entirely on this Mac. On macOS 27 voice notes open directly; a video's sound track and some containers (and, on older macOS, possibly voice notes) need ffmpeg. Basque and Catalan are not supported.

tools.name: calls_list
tools.description: Lists voice and video calls from WhatsApp's call history: when, how long, direction, missed or not, video or voice, group and participants. The outcome is the stored number, not a guessed meaning.

tools.name: location_sharing_list
tools.description: Lists live-location sharing sessions you started and who they were shared with. Coordinates are not decoded.

tools.name: labels_list
tools.description: Lists WhatsApp Business labels and how many chats carry each; with a label id, lists what carries it.

tools.name: address_book_list
tools.description: Looks up people in WhatsApp's own copy of your address book: names, business name, phone number, LID, username and about text.

tools.name: lid_lookup
tools.description: Given a LID or phone number, returns every pairing and name WhatsApp recorded for it, each labelled with the table it came from.

tools.name: channels_list
tools.description: Lists WhatsApp channels this Mac knows about: address, name and who added it.

tools.name: db_tables
tools.description: Lists the tables and views in one of WhatsApp's local databases (chat store, contacts, call history, labels, locations, stickers, status, channels and the rest). Names only, no rows.

tools.name: db_schema
tools.description: Returns the CREATE statements of one WhatsApp database, or of one table and its indexes. Structure only, no rows.

tools.name: db_query
tools.description: Runs one SELECT statement against one of WhatsApp's databases and returns the rows. Anything that is not a single read-only SELECT is refused; rows are capped and long statements are stopped.
